subject: Re: Model fit follow-up — quality regression after model update
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@acmeretail.com>; Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery + model fit follow-up

Hi Jane / Tom — great speaking with you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

Summary:
- Primary goal: improve product search relevance and auto-classification for returns, with target CTR uplift from 18% to ~25% and precision > 92% on the returns category.
- Current integration: Hosted API, model v2.0, batch size 16, prefix caching enabled.
- Recent change: we flagged that Redwood pushed a platform upgrade last week that rolled some customers to model variant v2.1. You mentioned you started seeing lower precision on a few test prompts.

Deliverables I said we'd follow up with:
1) Recommended model variants and quantization profiles for your workload (short-list).
2) Link to our benchmark diffs and the prompt sets we used for the evaluation.
3) A proposed playbook for pinning/rollback and a canary plan if you want to safely test v2.1.

I've attached the prompt sets we discussed (prompt-sets.xlsx) and a zip with the eval diffs (acme-model-eval.zip). Rachel will chime in with the technical diagnostics and the v2.0 vs v2.1 diff summary.

Next steps:
- Rachel: can you post the bench diffs and a short recommendation (pin/rollback/canary)?
- Jane: please share any failing prompt IDs or examples you want us to prioritize.
- I'll coordinate timing and, if needed, an expedited rollback for your production keys.

Thanks — available for a 30m follow-up tomorrow morning if you'd like to go over the diffs.

– Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: prompt-sets.xlsx, acme-model-eval.zip
From: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmeretail.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery + model fit follow-up

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. We pulled a few production examples after your call and confirmed regressions on ~4% of our returns auto-classification set. I attached a sample of the diffs (I clipped PII) and logged the failing prompt IDs in the sheet you sent.

Concerns / asks:
- This regression started after you mentioned model v2.1 was rolled to some hosted customers last Friday. We need a short-term mitigation (pin to v2.0) while we evaluate quality.
- Please confirm expected impact on rate limits/cost if we pin to v2.0 for our API key.
- We may also need a rollback window SLA — if rollback is required, can you estimate how quickly Redwood can revert our traffic?

We are looping in procurement if there will be any contract-level asks. For now, this is a high-priority quality/regression issue for our product team.

-Jane
Jane Sullivan
Sr. Product Manager, Search & Merchandising
Acme Retail
jane.sullivan@acmeretail.com

Attachment: version-diff-sample.json
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery + model fit follow-up

Hi Jane — thanks for the quick sample and the prompt IDs. I pulled your account's recent runs and compared v2.0 -> v2.1 across the classification and ranking suites referenced in prompt-sets.xlsx: 

Top-level findings:
- On average for your benchmark suite, recall is stable but precision dropped ~3.4pp on the returns category for v2.1 compared to v2.0 (we reproduced locally against your anonymized prompts).
- The degradation appears concentrated on prompts with long product descriptions + numeric-heavy content; likely an encoder normalization change in v2.1.

Immediate recommendation:
1) Pin your API key to v2.0 (we can do this server-side per-key). This will preserve current behavior and costs.
2) Open a canary rollout of v2.1 against 5% of traffic with strict monitoring (we can automatically compare outputs and rollback if the cohort sees >2pp precision drop).
3) Engineering plan: we'll run a targeted diff job against the failing prompt IDs you shared and return a per-prompt delta report within 48 hours.

Rollout mechanics & timeline:
- Pin to v2.0: 1–2 hours to apply and validate on hosted keys (no code changes on your side).
- Canary rollout: configurable; suggest 5% for 24–48 hours.
- Full rollback (if needed): we can revert traffic routing within 15 minutes of the decision if pinned is not acceptable (we'll coordinate a maintenance window if high throughput).

Links: benchmark diff report (internal): https://s3.redwood-internal.com/benchmarks/acme/2026-02/v2.0_vs_v2.1-report.html
Runbook: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/rollback-guides#pin-model-version

I'll attach the per-prompt diff script and the short regression checklist. If you want, we can schedule a technical call with our inference team to walk through the diffs and root cause.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (646) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-soc2.pdf (for procurement), per-prompt-diff-script.sh, regression-checklist.md
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 10:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery + model fit follow-up — quality regression after model update

Thanks Jane — glad we have a clear path. Quick operational plan and asks so everyone has expectations: 

Planned immediate actions:
- Today (within 2 hours): Redwood will pin Acme's API key to v2.0 and validate a smoke test (Rachel's team will confirm the results).
- +48 hours: Redwood runs targeted per-prompt diffs on the failing IDs and returns the delta report.
- Canary: if you approve, we'll enable a 5% v2.1 canary after diffs are reviewed (24–48h observation).

Questions for Acme:
- Can procurement confirm if any contract amendment is needed for an explicit pin/rollback SLA? If so, we can scope a short-term addendum.
- Please confirm the list of high-priority prompt IDs (we have the sheet but flag any additions).

Commitments from Redwood:
- No cost delta for keeping your key pinned to v2.0 in the short-term (we'll waive any per-variant charge for the duration of the investigation).
- We'll provide a runbook and the per-prompt regression report so your team can sign off on acceptance criteria before a broader rollout.

If that sounds good, I'll schedule a 30m technical review Monday at 10am PT with Rachel and our inference leads.

Best —
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Action items: pin key to v2.0 (Redwood), run diffs (Redwood), confirm procurement ask (Acme).
